509	    @staticmethod
510	    def _verified_lineage_entry(entry: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
511	        """Validate the linkage fields of one lineage chain entry."""
512	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
513	            return None
514	        dataset = entry.get("dataset")
515	        if not isinstance(dataset, str) or not dataset:
516	            return None
517	        version = entry.get("version")
518	        if not _is_int(version) or version < 1:
519	            return None
520	        source_version = entry.get("sourceVersion")
521	        if not _is_int(source_version) or source_version < 1:
522	            return None
523	        if not _is_hash(entry.get("sourceSha256")) or not _is_hash(entry.get("contentSha256")):
524	            return None
525	        row_count = entry.get("rowCount")
526	        if not _is_int(row_count) or row_count < 0:
527	            return None
528	        return entry

530	    def _lineage_issues(
531	        self, chain: Any, record: dict[str, Any], issues: list[dict[str, str]]
532	    ) -> None:
533	        if not isinstance(chain, list):
534	            issues.append({"code": "lineage", "message": "lineage must be an array"})
535	            return
536	        entries: list[dict[str, Any] | None] = []
537	        for index, raw_entry in enumerate(chain):
538	            entry = self._verified_lineage_entry(raw_entry)
539	            if entry is None:
540	                issues.append(
541	                    {
542	                        "code": "lineage",
543	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} is missing required fields "
544	                        "or uses invalid field types",
545	                    }
546	                )
547	            entries.append(entry)
548	
549	        for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
550	            if entry is None:
551	                continue
552	            if entry["dataset"] != record["dataset"]:
553	                issues.append(
554	                    {
555	                        "code": "lineage",
556	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} belongs to dataset "
557	                        f"{entry['dataset']!r}, expected {record['dataset']!r}",
558	                    }
559	                )
560	            if entry["sourceVersion"] >= entry["version"]:
561	                issues.append(
562	                    {
563	                        "code": "lineage",
564	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} has source version "
565	                        f"{entry['sourceVersion']} that is not below version {entry['version']}",
566	                    }
567	                )
568	
569	        for index in range(1, len(entries)):
570	            previous, current = entries[index - 1], entries[index]
571	            if previous is None or current is None:
572	                continue
573	            if current["sourceVersion"] != previous["version"]:
574	                issues.append(
575	                    {
576	                        "code": "lineage",
577	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} continues version "
578	                        f"{current['sourceVersion']} but the previous entry is version "
579	                        f"{previous['version']}",
580	                    }
581	                )
582	            elif current["sourceSha256"] != previous["contentSha256"]:
583	                issues.append(
584	                    {
585	                        "code": "lineage",
586	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} source hash does not match "
587	                        "the content hash of the previous entry",
588	                    }
589	                )
590	
591	        if entries:
592	            last = entries[-1]
593	            if last is not None:
594	                if last["version"] != record["version"]:
595	                    issues.append(
596	                        {
597	                            "code": "lineage",
598	                            "message": f"last lineage entry is version {last['version']} but "
599	                            f"the record is version {record['version']}",
600	                        }
601	                    )
602	                if last["contentSha256"] != record["content_sha256"]:
603	                    issues.append(
604	                        {
605	                            "code": "lineage",
606	                            "message": "last lineage entry content hash does not match the "
607	                            "record hash",
608	                        }
609	                    )
610	                if last["rowCount"] != record["row_count"]:
611	                    issues.append(
612	                        {
613	                            "code": "lineage",
614	                            "message": f"last lineage entry reports {last['rowCount']} records "
615	                            f"but the record reports {record['row_count']}",
616	                        }
617	                    )

619	    def verify_export(self, directory: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
620	        """Verify an exported directory offline against its manifest.
621	
622	        Only ``manifest.json`` and the CSV it names inside *directory* are
623	        read; no workspace state is consulted and nothing is written.
624	        Manifest or parameter problems raise ValueError, read failures
625	        OSError. Data discrepancies are returned as issue objects grouped
626	        by code: missing, hash, csv, rows, schema, lineage.
627	        """
628	        manifest_path = Path(directory) / "manifest.json"
629	        try:
630	            manifest_text = manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
631	        except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
632	            raise ValueError(f"manifest is not valid UTF-8: {error}") from error
633	        try:
634	            manifest = json.loads(manifest_text)
635	        except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
636	            raise ValueError(f"manifest is not valid JSON: {error}") from error
637	
638	        if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
639	            raise ValueError("manifest must be a JSON object")
640	        schema_version = manifest.get("schemaVersion")
641	        if not _is_int(schema_version) or schema_version != 1:
642	            raise ValueError("manifest schemaVersion must be the integer 1")
643	        if "record" not in manifest:
644	            raise ValueError("manifest is missing required field: record")
645	        if "file" not in manifest:
646	            raise ValueError("manifest is missing required field: file")
647	        record = self._verified_manifest_record(manifest["record"])
648	        file_name = manifest["file"]
649	        if (
650	            not isinstance(file_name, str)
651	            or not file_name
652	            or file_name in (".", "..")
653	            or "/" in file_name
654	            or "\\" in file_name
655	            or "\0" in file_name
656	        ):
657	            raise ValueError(
658	                "manifest file must be a non-empty file name without path separators"
659	            )
660	
661	        # Resolve purely lexically (no target content is read) and refuse
662	        # anything that escapes the export directory, including via links.
663	        base = Path(directory).resolve()
664	        try:
665	            resolved = (base / file_name).resolve(strict=False)
666	        except (OSError, RuntimeError):
667	            # Python 3.12 reports a symlink loop as RuntimeError. The
668	            # underlying message embeds a machine path and is intentionally
669	            # not surfaced.
670	            raise ValueError(
671	                f"manifest file {file_name!r} could not be safely resolved "
672	                "(broken or looping reference)"
673	            )
674	        if resolved != base and base not in resolved.parents:
675	            raise ValueError(
676	                f"manifest file {file_name!r} resolves outside the export directory"
677	            )
678	
679	        issues: list[dict[str, str]] = []
680	        lineage = manifest.get("lineage")
681	        if lineage is not None:
682	            # Missing or null lineage means no chain was shipped; an empty
683	            # array is likewise a chain-free (legacy) export.
684	            self._lineage_issues(lineage, record, issues)
685	
686	        if not resolved.exists():
687	            issues.append(
688	                {
689	                    "code": "missing",
690	                    "message": f"data file {file_name!r} listed in the manifest is missing",
691	                }
692	            )
693	        else:
694	            data = resolved.read_bytes()
695	            content_hash = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
696	            if content_hash != record["content_sha256"]:
697	                issues.append(
698	                    {
699	                        "code": "hash",
700	                        "message": "CSV content hash does not match the manifest record",
701	                    }
702	                )
703	
704	            header: list[str] | None = None
705	            rows: list[list[str]] = []
706	            header_ok = False
707	            records_ok = False
708	            can_parse = True
709	            try:
710	                text = data.decode("utf-8")
711	            except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
712	                issues.append(
713	                    {"code": "csv", "message": f"CSV is not valid UTF-8: {error.reason}"}
714	                )
715	                text = ""
716	                can_parse = False
717	            if can_parse and _ends_inside_quote(text):
718	                issues.append(
719	                    {"code": "csv", "message": "CSV has a quoted field that is never closed"}
720	                )
721	                can_parse = False
722	            if can_parse:
723	                parse_failed = False
724	                try:
725	                    # Non-strict parsing matches import semantics: only the
726	                    # explicitly enumerated structural problems are failures.
727	                    parsed = [
728	                        row
729	                        for row in csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
730	                        if row != []
731	                    ]
732	                except csv.Error as error:
733	                    issues.append(
734	                        {"code": "csv", "message": f"CSV structure is invalid: {error}"}
735	                    )
736	                    parsed = []
737	                    parse_failed = True
738	                if not parsed and not parse_failed:
739	                    issues.append({"code": "csv", "message": "CSV has no header row"})
740	                elif parsed:
741	                    header = parsed[0]
742	                    rows = parsed[1:]
743	                    empty_positions = [
744	                        position + 1 for position, name in enumerate(header) if name == ""
745	                    ]
746	                    if empty_positions:
747	                        issues.append(
748	                            {
749	                                "code": "csv",
750	                                "message": "CSV header has empty field name(s) at "
751	                                f"position(s) {empty_positions}",
752	                            }
753	                        )
754	                    seen: set[str] = set()
755	                    duplicates: list[str] = []
756	                    for name in header:
757	                        if name in seen and name not in duplicates:
758	                            duplicates.append(name)
759	                        seen.add(name)
760	                    if duplicates:
761	                        issues.append(
762	                            {
763	                                "code": "csv",
764	                                "message": "CSV header has duplicate field name(s): "
765	                                + ", ".join(repr(name) for name in duplicates),
766	                            }
767	                        )
768	                    header_ok = not empty_positions and not duplicates
769	                    ragged = [
770	                        row_number
771	                        for row_number, row in enumerate(rows, start=1)
772	                        if len(row) != len(header)
773	                    ]
774	                    if ragged:
775	                        issues.append(
776	                            {
777	                                "code": "csv",
778	                                "message": f"CSV record(s) {ragged} do not have the same "
779	                                f"number of fields as the header ({len(header)})",
780	                            }
781	                        )
782	                    records_ok = header_ok and not ragged
783	
784	            if header is not None:
785	                # Record numbering ignores blank physical lines and quoted
786	                # newlines already, so the count stays determinable even when
787	                # individual records are ragged.
788	                if len(rows) != record["row_count"]:
789	                    issues.append(
790	                        {
791	                            "code": "rows",
792	                            "message": f"CSV contains {len(rows)} data record(s) but the "
793	                            f"manifest record lists {record['row_count']}",
794	                        }
795	                    )
796	
797	            if header_ok:
798	                # The field set is fixed by the header and stays checkable
799	                # even when some data records are ragged.
800	                assert header is not None
801	                expected_schema = record["schema"]
802	                actual_fields = set(header)
803	                missing_fields = sorted(name for name in expected_schema if name not in actual_fields)
804	                extra_fields = sorted(name for name in actual_fields if name not in expected_schema)
805	                if missing_fields or extra_fields:
806	                    details = []
807	                    if missing_fields:
808	                        details.append("missing from CSV: " + ", ".join(missing_fields))
809	                    if extra_fields:
810	                        details.append("unexpected in CSV: " + ", ".join(extra_fields))
811	                    issues.append(
812	                        {
813	                            "code": "schema",
814	                            "message": "CSV field set does not match the manifest record ("
815	                            + "; ".join(details)
816	                            + ")",
817	                        }
818	                    )
819	                if records_ok:
820	                    # Type inference needs consistent column counts so each
821	                    # value can be aligned with its header position.
822	                    observed = {name: set() for name in header}
823	                    for row in rows:
824	                        for position, name in enumerate(header):
825	                            observed[name].add(_kind(row[position]))
826	                    inferred = {
827	                        name: _merge_kinds(kinds) for name, kinds in observed.items()
828	                    }
829	                    for name in sorted(expected_schema):
830	                        if name in inferred and inferred[name] != expected_schema[name]:
831	                            issues.append(
832	                                {
833	                                    "code": "schema",
834	                                    "message": f"field {name!r} infers as {inferred[name]!r} "
835	                                    f"but the manifest record declares "
836	                                    f"{expected_schema[name]!r}",
837	                                }
838	                            )
839	
840	        category_order = {
841	            "missing": 0,
842	            "hash": 1,
843	            "csv": 2,
844	            "rows": 3,
845	            "schema": 4,
846	            "lineage": 5,
847	        }
848	        issues.sort(key=lambda issue: category_order[issue["code"]])
849	        return {
850	            "dataset": record["dataset"],
851	            "version": record["version"],
852	            "passed": not issues,
853	            "issues": issues,
854	        }

857	    def _column_array(value: Any, where: str) -> list[str]:
858	        if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
859	            raise ValueError(f"{where} must be a non-empty array")
860	        if any(not isinstance(name, str) or not name for name in value):
861	            raise ValueError(f"{where} must contain only non-empty strings")
862	        if len(set(value)) != len(value):
863	            raise ValueError(f"{where} must not contain duplicates")
864	        return list(value)

866	    @classmethod
867	    def _validate_reference_payload(cls, rule: dict[str, Any], where: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
868	        misplaced = set(rule) - _REFERENCE_RULE_KEYS
869	        if misplaced:
870	            raise ValueError(f"{where} has unknown attributes: {sorted(misplaced)}")
871	        columns = cls._column_array(rule.get("columns"), f"{where}.columns")
872	        reference = rule.get("reference")
873	        if not isinstance(reference, dict):
874	            raise ValueError(f"{where}.reference must be an object")
875	        extra = set(reference) - _REFERENCE_KEYS
876	        if extra:
877	            raise ValueError(f"{where}.reference has unknown attributes: {sorted(extra)}")
878	        dataset = reference.get("dataset")
879	        if not isinstance(dataset, str) or not dataset:
880	            raise ValueError(f"{where}.reference.dataset must be a non-empty string")
881	        version = reference.get("version")
882	        if not _is_int(version) or version < 1:
883	            raise ValueError(f"{where}.reference.version must be a positive integer")
884	        ref_columns = cls._column_array(
885	            reference.get("columns"), f"{where}.reference.columns"
886	        )
887	        if len(columns) != len(ref_columns):
888	            raise ValueError(
889	                f"{where}.columns and {where}.reference.columns must have the same length"
890	            )
891	        return {
892	            "id": rule["id"],
893	            "type": "reference",
894	            "columns": columns,
895	            "reference": {
896	                "dataset": dataset,
897	                "version": version,
898	                "columns": ref_columns,
899	            },
900	        }

903	    def _validate_rules_payload(cls, rules: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
904	        if not isinstance(rules, list) or not rules:
905	            raise ValueError("rules must be a non-empty array")
906	        normalized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
907	        seen_ids: set[str] = set()
908	        for index, rule in enumerate(rules):
909	            where = f"rules[{index}]"
910	            if not isinstance(rule, dict):
911	                raise ValueError(f"{where} must be an object")
912	            extra = set(rule) - _RULE_KEYS
913	            if extra:
914	                raise ValueError(f"{where} has unknown attributes: {sorted(extra)}")
915	            identifier = rule.get("id")
916	            if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not identifier:
917	                raise ValueError(f"{where}.id must be a non-empty string")
918	            if identifier in seen_ids:
919	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate rule id: {identifier}")
920	            rule_type = rule.get("type")
921	            if rule_type not in _RULE_TYPES:
922	                raise ValueError(f"{where}.type must be one of {sorted(_RULE_TYPES)}")
923	            if rule_type == "reference":
924	                normalized.append(cls._validate_reference_payload(rule, where))
925	                seen_ids.add(identifier)
926	                continue
927	            misplaced = set(rule) & {"columns", "reference"}
928	            if misplaced:
929	                raise ValueError(f"{where} has unknown attributes: {sorted(misplaced)}")
930	            column = rule.get("column")
931	            if not isinstance(column, str) or not column:
932	                raise ValueError(f"{where}.column must be a non-empty column name")
933	            entry: dict[str, Any] = {"id": identifier, "column": column, "type": rule_type}
934	            if rule_type == "range":
935	                if "min" not in rule and "max" not in rule:
936	                    raise ValueError(f"{where} range requires min or max")
937	                bounds: dict[str, float] = {}
938	                for key in ("min", "max"):
939	                    if key not in rule:
940	                        continue
941	                    bound = rule[key]
942	                    # bool is a subclass of int; boundaries must be finite
943	                    # numbers rather than booleans.
944	                    if not isinstance(bound, (int, float)) or isinstance(bound, bool):
945	                        raise ValueError(f"{where}.{key} must be a finite number")
946	                    bound = float(bound)
947	                    if not math.isfinite(bound):
948	                        raise ValueError(f"{where}.{key} must be a finite number")
949	                    bounds[key] = bound
950	                if "min" in bounds and "max" in bounds and bounds["min"] > bounds["max"]:
951	                    raise ValueError(f"{where} min must not be greater than max")
952	                entry.update(bounds)
953	            elif "min" in rule or "max" in rule:
954	                raise ValueError(f"{where} bounds are only valid for range rules")
955	            seen_ids.add(identifier)
956	            normalized.append(entry)
957	        return normalized

959	    @staticmethod
960	    def _check_reference_targets(state: dict[str, Any], rules: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
961	        """Verify reference-rule targets against already stored versions.
962	
963	        The referenced dataset, version, and columns must all exist when the
964	        revision is created; the local columns are only checked when a data
965	        version is validated. Versions appended later on the reference side
966	        do not change what an existing revision points at.
967	        """
968	        for index, rule in enumerate(rules):
969	            if rule["type"] != "reference":
970	                continue
971	            where = f"rules[{index}].reference"
972	            reference = rule["reference"]
973	            target = reference["dataset"]
974	            versions = state["datasets"].get(target)
975	            if versions is None:
976	                raise ValueError(f"{where}.dataset names unknown dataset: {target}")
977	            version = reference["version"]
978	            if version > len(versions):
979	                raise ValueError(
980	                    f"{where}.version names unknown data version: {target}@{version}"
981	                )
982	            schema = versions[version - 1]["schema"]
983	            missing = [name for name in reference["columns"] if name not in schema]
984	            if missing:
985	                raise ValueError(
986	                    f"{where}.columns {missing} missing from {target}@{version}"
987	                )

989	    def set_rules(self, dataset: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
990	        state = self._load()
991	        if dataset not in state["datasets"]:
992	            raise ValueError(f"unknown dataset: {dataset}")
993	        normalized = self._validate_rules_payload(rules)
994	        # Checked before anything is appended, so a failed configuration
995	        # neither adds a revision nor consumes a revision number.
996	        self._check_reference_targets(state, normalized)
997	        history = state["rules"].setdefault(dataset, [])
998	        revision = len(history) + 1
999	        history.append(
1000	            {
1001	                "revision": revision,
1002	                "rules": normalized,
1003	                "set_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
1004	            }
1005	        )
1006	        self._save(state)
1007	        return {"dataset": dataset, "revision": revision, "rules": normalized}

1010	        history = state["rules"].get(dataset, [])
1011	        if not history:

1018	            entry = history[revision - 1]

1065	            # discards this report instead of leaving a partial entry behind.
1066	            stored.setdefault(str(version), {})[str(rule_revision)] = {
1067	                "content_sha256": content_hash,
1068	                "report": report,
1069	            }

1072	
1073	        blob_path = self.workspace / record["blob"]
1074	        if not blob_path.exists():
1075	            raise ValueError(f"stored data missing for {dataset}@{version}")
1076	        content_hash = _sha256(blob_path)
1077	        if content_hash != record["content_sha256"]:
1078	            raise ValueError(f"stored data hash mismatch for {dataset}@{version}")
1079

1101	                    result = results[rule["id"]]
1102	                    rule_type = rule["type"]

1159	        self,
1160	        state: dict[str, Any],
1161	        dataset: str,
1162	        version: int,
1163	        expected_hash: str | None = None,
1164	    ) -> tuple[str, list[str], list[list[str]]]:
1165	        """Re-verify and strictly parse one stored version, returning
1166	        ``(content_hash, header, rows)``.

1169	        given, a previously recorded hash), and the CSV structure are all
1170	        checked; every error names the dataset and version involved.
1171	        """

1173	        blob_path = self.workspace / record["blob"]
1174	        if not blob_path.exists():
1175	            raise ValueError(f"stored data missing for {dataset}@{version}")
1176	        content_hash = _sha256(blob_path)
1177	        if content_hash != record["content_sha256"]:
1178	            raise ValueError(f"stored data hash mismatch for {dataset}@{version}")
1179	        if expected_hash is not None and content_hash != expected_hash:
1180	            raise ValueError(f"stored data hash mismatch for {dataset}@{version}")

1186	            ) from error
1187	        except csv.Error as error:

1189	                f"stored CSV for {dataset}@{version} could not be parsed: {error}"
1190	            ) from error
1191	        return content_hash, header, rows

1193	    def _reference_sides(
1194	        self,
1195	        state: dict[str, Any],
1196	        dataset: str,
1197	        version: int,
1198	        rules: list[dict[str, Any]],
1199	        report: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
1200	    ) -> tuple[tuple[str, list[str], list[list[str]]], dict[tuple[str, int], tuple[str, list[str], list[list[str]]]]]:
1201	        """Load and verify the local side and every referenced side.
1202	
1203	        Returns ``(local, references)`` where ``local`` is the
1204	        ``(content_hash, header, rows)`` triple of the validated version and
1205	        ``references`` maps each referenced ``(dataset, version)`` to the
1206	        same triple. When ``report`` is given (a persisted report being
1207	        reused), each side's hash is additionally checked against the hash
1208	        recorded in that report. Field existence is verified on every call:
1209	        local columns against the selected version, reference columns
1210	        against their side.
1211	        """
1212	        expected_local = report["content_sha256"] if report is not None else None
1213	        local = self._load_verified_side(state, dataset, version, expected_local)
1214	        expected_reference: dict[tuple[str, int], str] = {}
1215	        if report is not None:
1216	            for item in report["results"]:
1217	                if item["type"] == "reference":
1218	                    reference = item["reference"]
1219	                    expected_reference[(reference["dataset"], reference["version"])] = (
1220	                        reference["content_sha256"]
1221	                    )
1222	        references: dict[tuple[str, int], tuple[str, list[str], list[list[str]]]] = {}
1223	        for rule in rules:
1224	            if rule["type"] != "reference":
1225	                continue
1226	            reference = rule["reference"]
1227	            key = (reference["dataset"], reference["version"])
1228	            if key in references:
1229	                continue
1230	            if key == (dataset, version):
1231	                references[key] = local
1232	            else:
1233	                references[key] = self._load_verified_side(
1234	                    state,
1235	                    reference["dataset"],
1236	                    reference["version"],
1237	                    expected_reference.get(key),
1238	                )
1239	        for rule in rules:
1240	            if rule["type"] == "reference":
1241	                local_names = rule["columns"]
1242	                reference = rule["reference"]
1243	                key = (reference["dataset"], reference["version"])
1244	                ref_header = references[key][1]
1245	                ref_names = reference["columns"]
1246	            else:
1247	                local_names = [rule["column"]]
1248	                ref_header = []
1249	                ref_names = []
1250	            for name in local_names:
1251	                if name not in local[1]:
1252	                    raise ValueError(f"missing column {name!r} for {dataset}@{version}")
1253	            for name in ref_names:
1254	                if name not in ref_header:
1255	                    raise ValueError(
1256	                        f"missing column {name!r} for "
1257	                        f"{reference['dataset']}@{reference['version']}"
1258	                    )
1259	        return local, references

1261	    def _validate_with_references(
1262	        self,
1263	        state: dict[str, Any],
1264	        dataset: str,
1265	        version: int,
1266	        rules: list[dict[str, Any]],
1267	        rule_revision: int,
1268	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
1269	        """Validate a version against a revision containing reference rules.
1270	
1271	        Both sides are strictly parsed. Combinations are matched on raw
1272	        strings — no trimming, no numeric conversion, and separators inside
1273	        values have no special meaning. Empty values or duplicate complete
1274	        combinations on a reference side fail the whole run, even when the
1275	        local side has no records.
1276	        """
1277	        (content_hash, header, rows), references = self._reference_sides(
1278	            state, dataset, version, rules
1279	        )
1280	
1281	        # Build each referenced combination set before scanning local rows,
1282	        # so reference-side problems surface even with zero local records.
1283	        combination_sets: dict[str, set[tuple[str, ...]]] = {}
1284	        for rule in rules:
1285	            if rule["type"] != "reference":
1286	                continue
1287	            reference = rule["reference"]
1288	            key = (reference["dataset"], reference["version"])
1289	            _, ref_header, ref_rows = references[key]
1290	            positions = [ref_header.index(name) for name in reference["columns"]]
1291	            combinations: set[tuple[str, ...]] = set()
1292	            for record_number, row in enumerate(ref_rows, start=1):
1293	                combination = tuple(row[position] for position in positions)
1294	                if any(part == "" for part in combination):
1295	                    raise ValueError(
1296	                        f"empty value in referenced column(s) of "
1297	                        f"{reference['dataset']}@{reference['version']} "
1298	                        f"record {record_number}"
1299	                    )
1300	                if combination in combinations:
1301	                    raise ValueError(
1302	                        f"duplicate complete combination in referenced "
1303	                        f"{reference['dataset']}@{reference['version']}"
1304	                    )
1305	                combinations.add(combination)
1306	            combination_sets[rule["id"]] = combinations
1307	
1308	        column_positions = {
1309	            rule["id"]: [
1310	                header.index(name)
1311	                for name in (
1312	                    rule["columns"] if rule["type"] == "reference" else [rule["column"]]
1313	                )
1314	            ]
1315	            for rule in rules
1316	        }
1317	        violations_by_id: dict[str, list[int]] = {rule["id"]: [] for rule in rules}
1318	        seen_unique: dict[str, dict[str, list[int]]] = {
1319	            rule["id"]: {} for rule in rules if rule["type"] == "unique"
1320	        }
1321	        for row_number, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
1322	            for rule in rules:
1323	                rule_type = rule["type"]
1324	                positions = column_positions[rule["id"]]
1325	                violations = violations_by_id[rule["id"]]
1326	                if rule_type == "required":
1327	                    if row[positions[0]] == "":
1328	                        violations.append(row_number)
1329	                elif rule_type == "unique":
1330	                    value = row[positions[0]]
1331	                    if value != "":
1332	                        seen_unique[rule["id"]].setdefault(value, []).append(row_number)
1333	                elif rule_type == "range":
1334	                    value = row[positions[0]]
1335	                    if value == "":
1336	                        continue
1337	                    number = _finite_number(value)
1338	                    if number is None or not (
1339	                        ("min" not in rule or number >= rule["min"])
1340	                        and ("max" not in rule or number <= rule["max"])
1341	                    ):
1342	                        violations.append(row_number)
1343	                else:  # reference
1344	                    combination = tuple(row[position] for position in positions)
1345	                    if (
1346	                        any(part == "" for part in combination)
1347	                        or combination not in combination_sets[rule["id"]]
1348	                    ):
1349	                        violations.append(row_number)
1350	
1351	        for rule_id, groups in seen_unique.items():
1352	            violations_by_id[rule_id] = sorted(
1353	                line for lines in groups.values() if len(lines) > 1 for line in lines
1354	            )
1355	
1356	        report_results = []
1357	        for rule in rules:
1358	            violations = violations_by_id[rule["id"]]
1359	            if rule["type"] == "reference":
1360	                reference = rule["reference"]
1361	                key = (reference["dataset"], reference["version"])
1362	                report_results.append(
1363	                    {
1364	                        "id": rule["id"],
1365	                        "type": "reference",
1366	                        "columns": list(rule["columns"]),
1367	                        "reference": {
1368	                            "dataset": reference["dataset"],
1369	                            "version": reference["version"],
1370	                            "columns": list(reference["columns"]),
1371	                            "content_sha256": references[key][0],
1372	                        },
1373	                        "violations": violations,
1374	                        "violationCount": len(violations),
1375	                    }
1376	                )
1377	            else:
1378	                report_results.append(
1379	                    {
1380	                        "id": rule["id"],
1381	                        "column": rule["column"],
1382	                        "type": rule["type"],
1383	                        "violations": violations,
1384	                        "violationCount": len(violations),
1385	                    }
1386	                )
1387	        total_violations = sum(item["violationCount"] for item in report_results)
1388	        report = {
1389	            "dataset": dataset,
1390	            "version": version,
1391	            "content_sha256": content_hash,
1392	            "rulesRevision": rule_revision,
1393	            "rowCount": len(rows),
1394	            "passed": total_violations == 0,
1395	            "results": report_results,
1396	        }
1397	        return report, content_hash

1420	    @staticmethod
1421	    def _validate_operations_payload(operations: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1422	        if not isinstance(operations, list) or not operations:
1423	            raise ValueError("operations must be a non-empty array")
1424	        normalized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1425	        for index, operation in enumerate(operations):
1426	            where = f"operations[{index}]"
1427	            if not isinstance(operation, dict):
1428	                raise ValueError(f"{where} must be an object")
1429	            operation_type = operation.get("type")
1430	            if operation_type not in _OPERATION_KEYS:
1431	                raise ValueError(f"{where}.type must be one of {sorted(_OPERATION_KEYS)}")
1432	            expected = _OPERATION_KEYS[operation_type]
1433	            if set(operation) != expected:
1434	                raise ValueError(f"{where} must have exactly the attributes {sorted(expected)}")
1435	            if operation_type in ("trim", "rename"):
1436	                if not isinstance(operation["column"], str) or not operation["column"]:

import csv as csv_module
import hashlib
import io
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from governance_workbench import Catalog
from governance_workbench.catalog import _read_csv_records

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def legacy_import(catalog: Catalog, dataset: str, contents: str) -> str:
    """Simulate a version stored by a pre-strictness build.

    Writes the bytes directly to the content-addressed blob directory and
    appends a catalog record using the old, permissive inference rules, so
    tests can exercise how downstream stages handle legacy ragged data
    without going through the now-strict importer.
    """
    import csv as csv_module
    import hashlib

    from governance_workbench.catalog import _kind, _merge_kinds

    data = contents.encode("utf-8")
    content_hash = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    catalog.blobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    blob = catalog.blobs / f"{content_hash}.csv"
    blob.write_bytes(data)

    reader = csv_module.DictReader(io.StringIO(contents, newline=""))
    fieldnames = reader.fieldnames or []
    observed = {name: set() for name in fieldnames}
    row_count = 0
    for row in reader:
        row_count += 1
        for name in fieldnames:
            observed[name].add(_kind(row[name] or ""))

    state = catalog._load()
    versions = state["datasets"].setdefault(dataset, [])
    versions.append(
        {
            "dataset": dataset,
            "version": len(versions) + 1,
            "source_name": "legacy.csv",
            "content_sha256": content_hash,
            "row_count": row_count,
            "schema": {name: _merge_kinds(kinds) for name, kinds in observed.items()},
            "imported_at": "2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
            "blob": str(blob.relative_to(catalog.workspace)),
        }
    )
    catalog._save(state)
    return content_hash


class CatalogTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def csv(self, name: str, contents: str) -> Path:
        path = self.root / name
        path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def test_import_infers_schema_and_preserves_blob(self):
        source = self.csv("input.csv", "id,active,score\n1,true,2.5\n2,false,3\n")
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("metrics", source)
        source.write_text("changed", encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(record.schema, {"id": "integer", "active": "boolean", "score": "number"})
        self.assertEqual(record.row_count, 2)
        self.assertNotEqual((self.catalog.workspace / record.blob).read_text(), "changed")

    def test_compare_reports_schema_and_row_changes(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("people", self.csv("one.csv", "id,name\n1,Ada\n"))
        self.catalog.import_csv("people", self.csv("two.csv", "id,name,region\n1,Ada,EU\n2,Lin,APAC\n"))
        result = self.catalog.compare("people", 1, 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["addedFields"], ["region"])
        self.assertEqual(result["rowDelta"], 1)
        self.assertTrue(result["contentChanged"])

    def test_export_manifest_matches_stored_content(self):
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("events", self.csv("events.csv", "id\n1\n"))
        destination = self.root / "export"
        manifest = self.catalog.export("events", 1, destination)
        on_disk = json.loads((destination / "manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(on_disk, manifest)
        self.assertEqual(manifest["record"]["content_sha256"], record.content_sha256)


class StrictImportTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def write(self, contents, name: str = "data.csv") -> Path:
        path = self.root / name
        if isinstance(contents, bytes):
            path.write_bytes(contents)
        else:
            path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def reject(self, contents):
        path = self.write(contents)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        return str(context.exception)

    # ---- validity rules with distinct reasons ----------------------------

    def test_invalid_files_rejected_with_distinct_reasons(self):
        cases = {
            "no header (empty file)": "",
            "empty header field": "a,\n1,2\n",
            "duplicate header field": "a,a\n1,2\n",
            "record too short": "a,b\n1\n",
            "record too long": "a,b\n1,2,3\n",
            "unclosed quote": 'a,b\n1,"unclosed\n',
        }
        messages = set()
        for label, contents in cases.items():
            message = self.reject(contents)
            self.assertTrue(message, label)
            self.assertNotIn(str(self.root), message)
            messages.add(message)
        self.assertEqual(len(messages), len(cases))

        # invalid UTF-8
        path = self.write(b"a,b\n1,\xff\n")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        self.assertIn("UTF-8", str(context.exception))
        messages.add(str(context.exception))

        # parse error: a field over the reader's size limit is a csv.Error
        path = self.write("a\n" + ("x" * 100) + "\n")
        previous_limit = csv_module.field_size_limit()
        try:
            csv_module.field_size_limit(10)
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
                self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        finally:
            csv_module.field_size_limit(previous_limit)
        self.assertIn("could not be parsed", str(context.exception))

    def test_field_count_error_names_record_number_actual_and_expected(self):
        # blank physical lines are skipped; the quoted newline stays in record 1,
        # so the ragged line is data record 2
        path = self.write('a,b\n\n1,"line one\nline two"\n2,3,4\n')
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        message = str(context.exception)
        self.assertIn("data record 2", message)
        self.assertIn("3 field(s)", message)
        self.assertIn("expected 2", message)

        # a short record reports its own number and actual count
        path = self.write("a,b,c\n1,2,3\n4\n")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        message = str(context.exception)
        self.assertIn("data record 2", message)
        self.assertIn("1 field(s)", message)
        self.assertIn("expected 3", message)

    # ---- accepted shapes --------------------------------------------------

    def test_header_only_file_imports_with_zero_rows_and_null_types(self):
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n"))
        self.assertEqual(record.row_count, 0)
        self.assertEqual(record.schema, {"a": "null", "b": "null"})
        rows = self.catalog.list_datasets()["d"]
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 1)

    def test_blank_lines_and_quoted_newlines_match_record_semantics(self):
        contents = 'id,name\n\n1,"line one\nline two"\n\n2,Bob\n'
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(contents))
        self.assertEqual(record.row_count, 2)

    def test_empty_vs_whitespace_inference_and_quote_then_text_kept(self):
        record = self.catalog.import_csv(
            "d", self.write("id,v,w\n1,,s\n2, ,\"x\"y\n")
        )
        # "" is missing/null, " " is a whitespace string; "x"y parses as xy
        self.assertEqual(record.schema, {"id": "integer", "v": "string", "w": "string"})
        _, rows = _read_csv_records((self.catalog.workspace / record.blob).read_bytes())
        self.assertEqual(rows[0][1], "")
        self.assertEqual(rows[1][1], " ")
        self.assertEqual(rows[1][2], "xy")

    def test_stored_bytes_match_source_exactly(self):
        contents = 'id,name\r\n1, "Ada" \r\n2,"line one\nline two"\r\n'
        source = self.write(contents)
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        stored = (self.catalog.workspace / record.blob).read_bytes()
        # newlines, spacing and quoting are preserved byte-for-byte
        self.assertEqual(stored, contents.encode("utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(record.content_sha256, hashlib.sha256(stored).hexdigest())

    def test_later_source_change_does_not_affect_version(self):
        source = self.write("id,v\n1,5\n")
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        source.write_text("id,v\n9,999\n", encoding="utf-8")
        reloaded = Catalog(self.catalog.workspace)
        stored = (reloaded.workspace / record.blob).read_bytes()
        self.assertEqual(stored, b"id,v\n1,5\n")
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.get("d", 1)["content_sha256"], record.content_sha256)

    def test_source_replaced_during_import_cannot_desynchronize_version(self):
        # The file on disk (B, ragged) differs from the bytes the importer
        # snapshots at read time (A). The stored blob and record must both
        # describe A; the old code re-read the path while copying and ended
        # up storing B under A's description.
        valid = b"id,v\n1,5\n"
        source = self.write(b"id,v\n1,5,extra\n")
        real_open = Path.open

        def snapshot_open(path, *args, **kwargs):
            if Path(path) == source:
                return io.BytesIO(valid)
            return real_open(path, *args, **kwargs)

        with mock.patch.object(Path, "open", snapshot_open):
            record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        stored = (self.catalog.workspace / record.blob).read_bytes()
        self.assertEqual(stored, valid)
        self.assertEqual(record.content_sha256, hashlib.sha256(valid).hexdigest())
        export_dir = self.root / "out"
        self.catalog.export("d", 1, export_dir)
        self.assertTrue(Catalog(self.root / "offline").verify_export(export_dir)["passed"])

    # ---- content-addressed storage ---------------------------------------

    def test_repeated_imports_append_versions_but_share_blob(self):
        source = self.write("id,v\n1,5\n")
        first = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        second = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        third = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        self.assertEqual([r["version"] for r in self.catalog.list_datasets()["d"]], [1, 2, 3])
        self.assertEqual({first.blob, second.blob, third.blob}, {first.blob})
        self.assertEqual(
            first.content_sha256,
            self.catalog.get("d", 3)["content_sha256"],
        )

    def test_existing_matching_blob_is_reused(self):
        data = b"id,v\n1,5\n"
        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        self.catalog.blobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        existing = self.catalog.blobs / f"{content_hash}.csv"
        existing.write_bytes(data)
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(data.decode("utf-8")))
        self.assertEqual(record.blob, str(existing.relative_to(self.catalog.workspace)))
        self.assertEqual(existing.read_bytes(), data)

    def test_corrupt_existing_blob_errors_and_is_not_overwritten(self):
        data = b"id,v\n1,5\n"
        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        self.catalog.blobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        damaged = self.catalog.blobs / f"{content_hash}.csv"
        damaged.write_bytes(b"id,v\n9,9\n")
        with self.assertRaises(OSError):
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(data.decode("utf-8")))
        # the corrupt file is untouched and no version appeared
        self.assertEqual(damaged.read_bytes(), b"id,v\n9,9\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.list_datasets(), {})
        # once storage is repaired, reuse succeeds
        damaged.write_bytes(data)
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(data.decode("utf-8")))
        self.assertEqual(record.version, 1)
        self.assertEqual(record.content_sha256, content_hash)

    # ---- failure atomicity ------------------------------------------------

    def test_invalid_data_creates_nothing_and_consumes_no_version(self):
        self.reject("a,b\n1,2,3\n")
        self.assertFalse(self.catalog.state_path.exists())
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.list_datasets(), {})
        # no stray temporary files in the blob directory
        leftovers = list(self.catalog.blobs.glob("*.tmp")) if self.catalog.blobs.exists() else []
        self.assertEqual(leftovers, [])
        # retry uses the original next version number
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n1,2\n", "good.csv"))
        self.assertEqual(record.version, 1)

    def test_failed_import_after_good_version_consumes_no_version(self):

    def test_blob_write_failure_leaves_no_blob_and_no_version(self):

        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n1,2\n"))
        self.assertEqual(record.version, 1)

    def test_state_write_failure_leaves_no_version_but_blob_remains(self):
        with mock.patch.object(Catalog, "_save", side_effect=OSError("disk full")):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):

        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.list_datasets(), {})
        # the orphaned blob is content-addressed and verified on reuse

    def test_missing_and_unreadable_source_raise_oserror(self):

        source = self.write("a,b\n1,2\n")

        def deny_open(path, *args, **kwargs):

        with mock.patch.object(Path, "open", deny_open):

        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.list_datasets(), {})

    def test_failed_import_invisible_after_restart(self):
        self.reject("a,b\n1,2,3\n")
        reloaded = Catalog(self.catalog.workspace)
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.list_datasets(), {})

    # ---- round trip --------------------------------------------------------

    def test_imported_version_exports_and_verifies(self):

class RulesConfigurationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")
        source = self.root / "things.csv"
        source.write_text("id,v\n1,5\n", encoding="utf-8")
        self.catalog.import_csv("things", source)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def test_valid_rule_shapes(self):
        result = self.catalog.set_rules(
            "things",
            [
                {"id": "r1", "column": "id", "type": "required"},
                {"id": "r2", "column": "id", "type": "unique"},
                {"id": "r3", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": 0},
                {"id": "r4", "column": "v", "type": "range", "max": 10},
                {"id": "r5", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": -1.5, "max": 10.5},
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(result["revision"], 1)
        self.assertEqual([rule["id"] for rule in result["rules"]], ["r1", "r2", "r3", "r4", "r5"])

    def test_revisions_are_contiguous_and_immutable(self):
        first = self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        second = self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "b", "column": "v", "type": "unique"}])
        self.assertEqual((first["revision"], second["revision"]), (1, 2))
        state = json.loads(self.catalog.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(state["rules"]["things"][0]["rules"][0]["id"], "a")
        self.assertEqual(state["rules"]["things"][1]["rules"][0]["id"], "b")

    def test_unknown_dataset_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.set_rules("missing", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])

    def test_invalid_configurations(self):
        def reject(rules):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.set_rules("things", rules)

        reject([])
        reject("not-a-list")
        reject([None])
        reject(["not-an-object"])
        reject([{"column": "id", "type": "required"}])  # missing id
        reject([{"id": "", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])  # empty id
        reject([{"id": 5, "column": "id", "type": "required"}])  # non-string id
        reject([{"id": "a"}])  # missing column and type
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "", "type": "required"}])  # empty column
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": 7, "type": "required"}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "mystery"}])  # unknown type
        reject(
            [
                {"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"},
                {"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "unique"},  # duplicate id
            ]
        )
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required", "extra": 1}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range"}])  # no bounds
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": 10, "max": 1}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": True}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "max": False}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": "1"}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": float("nan")}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "max": float("inf")}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required", "min": 1}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "unique", "max": 1}])

    def test_failed_write_does_not_consume_revision_and_retry_succeeds(self):
        with mock.patch.object(Catalog, "_save", side_effect=OSError("disk full")):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        state = json.loads(self.catalog.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(state.get("rules", {}).get("things", []), [])
        result = self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        self.assertEqual(result["revision"], 1)

    def test_works_with_legacy_workspace_state(self):
        state_path = self.catalog.state_path
        state = json.loads(state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        del state["rules"]
        del state["validations"]
        state_path.write_text(json.dumps(state), encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        self.assertEqual(result["revision"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.validate("things", 1)["passed"], True)


class ValidationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def csv_file(self, contents: str, name: str = "data.csv") -> Path:
        path = self.root / name
        path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def test_required_unique_range_semantics(self):
        csv_contents = (
            "id,v,label\n"
            "1,0,a\n"          # row 1: in range, unique values so far
            "2,10,a\n"         # row 2: boundary max included; duplicate label
            "3,-1,b\n"         # row 3: below min
            "4,11, c\n"        # row 4: above max
            "5,,\n"            # row 5: missing v skipped by range, missing label
            "6,abc,d\n"        # row 6: non-numeric
            "7,true,e\n"       # row 7: boolean-looking cell is not a number
            "8,inf,f\n"        # row 8: non-finite
            "9,nan,g\n"        # row 9: non-finite
            "10, 5,h\n"        # row 10: whitespace is not stripped
            "11,5.0,i\n"       # row 11: finite numeric passes
            "12,1e1,j\n"       # row 12: 10.0 passes (max inclusive)
            " ,0,k\n"          # row 13: whitespace id is present and distinct
        )
        self.catalog.import_csv("things", self.csv_file(csv_contents))
        self.catalog.set_rules(
            "things",
            [
                {"id": "id-required", "column": "id", "type": "required"},
                {"id": "label-unique", "column": "label", "type": "unique"},
                {"id": "v-range", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": 0, "max": 10},
            ],
        )
        report = self.catalog.validate("things", 1)
        by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in report["results"]}
        self.assertEqual([item["id"] for item in report["results"]],
                         ["id-required", "label-unique", "v-range"])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["id-required"]["violations"], [])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["label-unique"]["violations"], [1, 2])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["v-range"]["violations"], [3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["v-range"]["violationCount"], 7)
        self.assertFalse(report["passed"])
        self.assertEqual(report["rowCount"], 13)
        self.assertTrue(all(
            item["violations"] == sorted(item["violations"])
            for item in report["results"]
        ))

    def test_quoted_newline_does_not_advance_row_number(self):
        csv_contents = "id,name\n1,\"line one\nline two\"\n2,\n"
        self.catalog.import_csv("notes", self.csv_file(csv_contents))
        self.catalog.set_rules(
            "notes",
            [
                {"id": "name-required", "column": "name", "type": "required"},
                {"id": "name-unique", "column": "name", "type": "unique"},
            ],
        )
        report = self.catalog.validate("notes", 1)
        by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in report["results"]}
        self.assertEqual(report["rowCount"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(by_id["name-required"]["violations"], [2])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["name-unique"]["violations"], [])

    def test_empty_string_missing_but_whitespace_present(self):

    def test_validate_does_not_modify_data_or_add_versions(self):
        source = self.csv_file("v\n1\n")

class ReferenceRuleTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):

        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")

    def tearDown(self):

    def csv_file(self, contents: str, name: str = "data.csv") -> Path:

        path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")

    def import_reference_side(self):

        )

    def reference_rule(self, **overrides):
        rule = {
            "id": "客户引用",
            "type": "reference",
            "columns": ["客户号", "地区"],
            "reference": {"dataset": "客户", "version": 2, "columns": ["编号", "地区"]},
        }
        rule.update(overrides)
        return rule

    # ---- configuration ---------------------------------------------------

    def test_valid_reference_rule_configuration(self):

        self.catalog.import_csv("orders", self.csv_file("客户号,地区\nC1,北\n", "orders.csv"))

        self.assertEqual(rule["type"], "reference")
        self.assertEqual(rule["columns"], ["客户号", "地区"])
        self.assertEqual(
            rule["reference"],
            {"dataset": "客户", "version": 2, "columns": ["编号", "地区"]},

                }
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(result["revision"], 1)
        self.assertTrue(self.catalog.validate("d", 1)["passed"])

    def test_invalid_reference_configurations(self):
        self.import_reference_side()
        self.catalog.import_csv("orders", self.csv_file("客户号,地区\nC1,北\n", "orders.csv"))

        def reject(rule):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.set_rules("orders", [rule])

        reject({"id": "r", "type": "reference",
                "reference": {"dataset": "客户", "version": 2, "columns": ["编号"]}})  # no columns
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference=None))  # missing reference object
        reject(self.reference_rule(extra=1))  # extra attribute
        reject(self.reference_rule(column="客户号"))  # single-column form not allowed
        reject(self.reference_rule(min=1))
        reject(self.reference_rule(max=2))
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=[]))  # empty columns
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns="客户号"))  # not an array
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=["客户号", ""]))  # empty name
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=["客户号", 7]))  # non-string
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=["客户号", "客户号"]))  # duplicates
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"], "x": 1}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"version": 2, "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": 5, "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户",
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))  # no version
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 0,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": -1,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": True,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2.0,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": []}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "编号"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号"]}))  # unequal lengths
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=["客户号"],
                                   reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        # old rule types reject the new attributes
        reject({"id": "r", "column": "客户号", "type": "required", "columns": ["客户号"]})
        reject({"id": "r", "column": "客户号", "type": "unique",
                "reference": {"dataset": "客户", "version": 2, "columns": ["编号"]}})
        # id uniqueness still applies across mixed types
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.set_rules(
                "orders",
                [
                    self.reference_rule(),
                    {"id": "客户引用", "column": "地区", "type": "required"},
                ],
            )

    def test_report_persists_and_revalidation_rechecks_every_side(self):
        self.import_reference_side()
        self.catalog.import_csv("orders", self.csv_file("客户号,地区\nC1,北\nC9,北\n", "orders.csv"))
        self.catalog.set_rules("orders", [self.reference_rule()])
        first = self.catalog.validate("orders", 1)
        second = self.catalog.validate("orders", 1)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        # exactly one report persisted, retrievable after a restart
        reloaded = Catalog(self.catalog.workspace)
        history = reloaded.validation_history("orders", 1)
        self.assertEqual(history, [first])
        state = json.loads(self.catalog.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(len(state["validations"]["orders"]["1"]), 1)

        # tampering with the reference side is noticed on revalidation
        reference_record = self.catalog.get("客户", 2)
        reference_blob = self.catalog.workspace / reference_record["blob"]
        reference_original = reference_blob.read_bytes()
        reference_blob.write_text("编号,地区,备注\nC1,北,x\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            reloaded.validate("orders", 1)
        self.assertIn("客户@2", str(context.exception))
        reference_blob.write_bytes(reference_original)

        # tampering with the local side is noticed as well
        local_record = self.catalog.get("orders", 1)
        local_blob = self.catalog.workspace / local_record["blob"]
        local_original = local_blob.read_bytes()
        local_blob.write_text("客户号,地区\nC1,北\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            reloaded.validate("orders", 1)
        self.assertIn("orders@1", str(context.exception))
        local_blob.write_bytes(local_original)

        # a missing reference file fails the run without touching the report
        reference_blob.unlink()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            reloaded.validate("orders", 1)
        self.assertIn("客户@2", str(context.exception))
        reference_blob.write_bytes(reference_original)
        # the stored report survived every failed revalidation unchanged
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.validation_history("orders", 1), [first])
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.validate("orders", 1), first)

class CleanTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")
        self.catalog.import_csv(
            "people",
            self.csv_file(
                "id,name,city\n"
                "1, Ada ,x\n"
                "2,Bob,y\n"
                "1, Ada ,x\n"
                "3,Ada,z\n"
            ),
        )

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def csv_file(self, contents: str, name: str = "data.csv") -> Path:
        path = self.root / name
        path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def ops_file(self, operations, name: str = "ops.json") -> Path:
        path = self.root / name
        path.write_text(json.dumps(operations), encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def clean_people(self):
        return self.catalog.clean(
            "people",
            1,
            [
                {"type": "trim", "column": "name"},
                {"type": "rename", "column": "city", "to": "region"},
                {"type": "drop_duplicates", "columns": ["id", "name"]},
            ],
        )

    def test_clean_appends_version_with_result_shape(self):
        result = self.clean_people()
        self.assertEqual(result["version"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["row_count"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(result["schema"], {"id": "integer", "name": "string", "region": "string"})
        stored = (self.catalog.workspace / result["blob"]).read_bytes()
        self.assertEqual(stored, b"id,name,region\n1,Ada,x\n2,Bob,y\n3,Ada,z\n")
        # the source version is untouched
        self.assertEqual(len(self.catalog.list_datasets()["people"]), 2)
        original = self.catalog.get("people", 1)
        self.assertEqual(original["row_count"], 4)

    def test_cleaned_version_supports_compare_validate_export(self):
        self.clean_people()
        comparison = self.catalog.compare("people", 1, 2)
        self.assertEqual(comparison["addedFields"], ["region"])
        self.assertEqual(comparison["removedFields"], ["city"])
        self.assertEqual(comparison["rowDelta"], -1)
        self.catalog.set_rules("people", [{"id": "r", "column": "name", "type": "required"}])
        report = self.catalog.validate("people", 2)
        self.assertTrue(report["passed"])
        self.assertEqual(report["rowCount"], 3)
        manifest = self.catalog.export("people", 2, self.root / "out")
        self.assertEqual(manifest["record"]["version"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(manifest["file"], "people-v2.csv")
        self.assertEqual(len(manifest["lineage"]), 1)

    def test_lineage_records_steps_rows_and_columns(self):
        self.clean_people()
        lineage = self.catalog.lineage("people", 2)
        self.assertEqual(lineage["dataset"], "people")
        self.assertEqual(lineage["version"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(lineage["chain"]), 1)
        entry = lineage["chain"][0]
        self.assertEqual(entry["sourceVersion"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(entry["sourceSha256"], self.catalog.get("people", 1)["content_sha256"])
        self.assertEqual(
            entry["operations"],
            [
                {"type": "trim", "column": "name"},
                {"type": "rename", "column": "city", "to": "region"},
                {"type": "drop_duplicates", "columns": ["id", "name"]},
            ],
        )
        steps = entry["steps"]
        self.assertEqual([(s["inputRows"], s["outputRows"]) for s in steps], [(4, 4), (4, 4), (4, 3)])
        self.assertEqual(steps[0]["modifiedRows"], [1, 3])
        self.assertEqual((steps[1]["from"], steps[1]["to"]), ("city", "region"))
        self.assertEqual(steps[2]["deletedRows"], [3])
        self.assertEqual(entry["columnMapping"], {"id": "id", "name": "name", "region": "city"})
        self.assertEqual(entry["rowMapping"], [1, 2, 4])

    def test_quoted_newline_does_not_count_as_record(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("notes", self.csv_file("id,name\n1,\"line one\nline two\"\n2, x \n", "notes.csv"))
        result = self.catalog.clean("notes", 1, [{"type": "trim", "column": "name"}])
        entry = result["lineage"]
        self.assertEqual(entry["steps"][0]["modifiedRows"], [2])
        self.assertEqual(entry["rowMapping"], [1, 2])

    def test_dedup_uses_raw_strings_and_empty_strings_participate(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("raw", self.csv_file("a,b\n1,\n01,\n1,\n", "raw.csv"))
        result = self.catalog.clean("raw", 1, [{"type": "drop_duplicates", "columns": ["a", "b"]}])
        # "1" and "01" are distinct strings; the second ("1", "") is dropped
        self.assertEqual(result["lineage"]["steps"][0]["deletedRows"], [3])
        self.assertEqual(result["lineage"]["rowMapping"], [1, 2])

    def test_repeat_clean_is_deterministic_but_appends(self):
        first = self.clean_people()
        second = self.clean_people()
        self.assertEqual((first["version"], second["version"]), (2, 3))
        self.assertEqual(first["content_sha256"], second["content_sha256"])
        self.assertEqual(first["blob"], second["blob"])
        self.assertEqual(first["lineage"]["rowMapping"], second["lineage"]["rowMapping"])
        self.assertEqual(first["lineage"]["steps"], second["lineage"]["steps"])

    def test_noop_and_header_only_cleans_still_append(self):
        noop = self.catalog.clean("people", 1, [{"type": "trim", "column": "id"}])
        self.assertEqual(noop["row_count"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(noop["lineage"]["steps"][0]["modifiedRows"], [])
        self.catalog.import_csv("empty", self.csv_file("a,b\n", "empty.csv"))
        header_only = self.catalog.clean("empty", 1, [{"type": "trim", "column": "a"}])
        self.assertEqual(header_only["row_count"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(header_only["lineage"]["rowMapping"], [])

    def test_chain_extends_across_cleans_and_survives_restart(self):
        self.clean_people()
        self.catalog.clean("people", 2, [{"type": "rename", "column": "region", "to": "area"}])
        reloaded = Catalog(self.catalog.workspace)
        lineage = reloaded.lineage("people", 3)
        self.assertEqual([entry["version"] for entry in lineage["chain"]], [2, 3])
        self.assertEqual(lineage["chain"][0]["sourceVersion"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(lineage["chain"][1]["sourceVersion"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(lineage["chain"][1]["columnMapping"]["area"], "region")
        # an imported version is the chain start
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.lineage("people", 1)["chain"], [])

    def test_export_of_imported_version_has_no_lineage(self):
        manifest = self.catalog.export("people", 1, self.root / "plain")
        self.assertNotIn("lineage", manifest)

    def test_invalid_operations_rejected_without_version(self):
        def reject(operations):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.clean("people", 1, operations)

        reject([])
        reject(42)
        reject({"type": "trim", "column": "name"})  # payload must be an array
        reject([None])
        reject([{"column": "name"}])  # missing type
        reject([{"type": "sort", "column": "name"}])  # unknown operation

        reject([{"type": "trim", "column": "name", "extra": 1}])  # extra attribute
        reject([{"type": "trim", "column": ""}])
        reject([{"type": "trim", "column": 3}])
